business_problem: turbopuffer needed a search architecture for AI applications that could store every byte of data cheaply while still delivering strongly consistent vector and full-text queries at scale.
solution_summary: turbopuffer uses Google Cloud to address this challenge: turbopuffer needed a search architecture for AI applications that could store every byte of data cheaply while still delivering strongly consistent vector and full-text queries at scale. Google Cloud Storage serves as the only storage dependency for the database and uses Compare-and-Swap semantics to preserve distributed consistency, serving as the storage layer. Google Kubernetes Engine simplifies management of the containerized application layer around the search system, serving as the orchestration layer. Compute Engine launches virtual machines on demand for the high-performance search service, serving as the compute layer. Vector and full-text data is stored directly in Google Cloud Storage, the search engine coordinates access through cloud-storage primitives instead of an external database, and GKE plus Compute Engine supply the execution environment for query-serving workloads.
